feedback.problem: Given $P(A)=\frac{1}{3}$, $P(B)=\frac{3}{8}$, $P(A\cup B)=\frac{17}{24}$, determine whether $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
feedback.worked_solution:
To check if $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive, we must check that $P(A\cap B)=0.$

We can calculate $P(A\cap B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{17}{24} & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{3}{8}-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =\frac{1}{3}+\frac{3}{8}-\frac{17}{24} \\  & =\frac{8+9-17}{24}=0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events.
